syntax: SELECT ... FROM sizes CROSS JOIN colors
summary: Produce every combination of rows from two tables.
documentation: CROSS JOIN forms a Cartesian product: each left row pairs with every right row. A set of m sizes and n colors therefore produces m times n combinations, without requiring a matching key.
inputs: sizes(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, label TEXT) and colors(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, label TEXT).
returns: size_id and color_id for every combination, sorted by size_id then color_id.
caution: The result grows multiplicatively and is empty if either input is empty. Use it for deliberate combinations; accidentally omitting a join condition in other queries can create this same expansion.
scenarios: Preview every size-and-color variant of a small product set.
Generate all local test combinations for two option lists.
Create a scheduling grid from available rooms and time slots.
title: Generate every variant pair
problem: Return sizes.id AS size_id and colors.id AS color_id for every size/color combination. Order by size_id, color_id. Pair rows by identity even when labels are identical or NULL.
hint: Use CROSS JOIN without a matching condition, and qualify both id columns.
goal: Use CROSS JOIN or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
